## Design

### 2026-11-03: I started planning the DicePopper. I did what I have done for all of the other projects and sketched up a design in a notebook. I also wrote a quick BOM on the other side. It is accurate to my project

**2h**

I started planning the DicePopper. I did what I have done for all of the other projects and sketched up a design in a notebook. I also wrote a quick BOM on the other side. It is accurate to my project except for information on solenoids. I couldn't find any available solenoids in NZ that use the right voltage/wattage, and are capable of popping up the plate.

![WIN_20261104_17_05_26_Pro](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/77fc6a190d52f92e453c526fedfb56760970b35133c38313d27530db2ed8d625.jpg)

![WIN_20261104_17_05_38_Pro](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/818c4c63aa857568752a97dabddb3d097c5bf061282b45f995e9a56aa578e280.jpg)

I have also been researching ways to lift and drop the plate effectively. I need it to use 5V and preferably not use many mechanical systems. I am considering using a few servo motors or a piston with a stepper. I am going to continue looking for options but I might start on other parts before I have decided. I found a cool website with mechanical systems and played around with them. It's called 507movements.com.
